     9	/-!
    10	# DJ-0: quasi-compactness from a compact-space source via a surjection
    11	
    12	The smallest, ungated brick of the DAT-J worksheet (`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
    13	§2.4): the abstract topological shape that `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes to get
    14	quasi-compactness of the Jacobian structure morphism from the Abel image of `Div^g`-lite.
    15	
    16	The mathematics is entirely mathlib's: the continuous surjective image of a compact space
    17	is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). This file packages that for scheme
    18	morphisms and adds the quasi-compactness corollary over an affine base, so DAT-J's qc
    19	field is a one-line instantiation. It is deliberately **Challenge-free** (mathlib-only, no
    20	curve/Challenge imports) — the DAT-J producer cone must not cycle through `Challenge.lean`
    21	(worksheet §0.5 / risk 1).
    22	
    23	## Main results
    24	
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_surjective`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of
    26	  schemes out of a compact-space source `X`, then `Y` is a compact space.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective`: a structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an
    28	  affine base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives such a surjection. This is the
    29	  shape DAT-J's DJ-1 consumes with `X := Div^g` (`compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel`
    30	  the Abel morphism, `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	set_option autoImplicit false
    34	
    35	universe u
    36	
    37	open CategoryTheory
    38	
    39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    40	
    41	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    42	
    43	/-- **DJ-0, compact-image half.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of schemes out of a
    44	compact-space source, then the target is a compact space: the underlying map of `f` is a
    45	continuous surjection (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`), and the continuous surjective image of a
    46	compact space is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). -/
    47	theorem compactSpace_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X]
    48	    (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : CompactSpace Y :=
    49	  hf.compactSpace f.continuous
    50	
    51	/-- **DJ-0, quasi-compactness corollary.** A structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an affine
    52	base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives a surjection `f : X ⟶ Y` from a
    53	compact-space source `X`. Over an affine base, `QuasiCompact g` is exactly `CompactSpace Y`
    54	(`HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine`, the `DivSchemeQProj` pattern), which the
    55	compact-image half supplies.
    56	
    57	This is the abstract shape `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes: instantiate
    58	`X := Div^g` (compact via `compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel` the Abel morphism
    59	(surjective on points, DJ-1), `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`. -/
    60	theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsAffine Z]
    61	    [CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : QuasiCompact g :=
    62	  haveI : CompactSpace Y := compactSpace_of_surjective f hf
    63	  HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
    64	
    65	end AlgebraicGeometry

    70	/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
    71	admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
    72	underlying map of `f` is surjective.
    73	
    74	`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
    75	is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
    76	of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.
    77	
    78	This is the missing link between what the Picard side produces and what DAT-J's
    79	quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
    80	a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
    81	spaces. -/
    82	theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
    83	    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
    84	      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
    85	    Function.Surjective f.base := by
    86	  intro y
    87	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
    88	  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
    89	  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
    90	  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
    91	  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
    92	  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
    93	  exact hs
    94	
    95	end Topology

    13	/-!
    14	# Representability of `Pic^0` over a separably closed field
    15	
    16	This module turns the public rank-one open and the translated field-point theorem into the
    17	Zariski atlas required by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  The chart source is the actual open of
    18	the genus divisor representer supplied by `DivRankOneOpenData`; its map to the rank-one locus is
    19	the canonical Abel isomorphism, and each chart is translated by the same base class that indexes
    20	it.

    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	
    41	noncomputable section
    42	
    43	/-! ## Sigma-extension isomorphisms -/
    44	
    45	/-- Sigma extension preserves natural isomorphisms of slice presheaves. -/
    46	noncomputable def sigmaExtensionIso {F G : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    47	    (e : F ≅ G) :
    48	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F ≅
    49	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) G where
    50	  hom := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.hom
    51	  inv := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.inv
    52	  hom_inv_id := by
    53	    ext T x
    54	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    55	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.hom_inv_id_app_apply _ x)
    56	  inv_hom_id := by
    57	    ext T x
    58	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    59	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.inv_hom_id_app_apply _ x)
    60	
    61	/-- A representation on the slice extends to an isomorphism between the ambient Yoneda
    62	presheaf of its representing object and the sigma extension. -/
    63	noncomputable def representableBySigmaIso
    64	    {F : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    65	    (rep : F.RepresentableBy J) :
    66	    yoneda.obj J.left ≅ Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F where
    67	  hom := rep.toSigmaExtension
    68	  inv :=
    69	    { app := fun T => TypeCat.ofHom fun x => (rep.homEquiv.symm x.2).left
    70	      naturality := by
    71	        intro T T' f
    72	        ext x
    73	        rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    74	        let q : Over.mk (f.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a := Over.homMk f.unop rfl
    75	        exact (congrArg Over.Hom.left
    76	          (rep.comp_homEquiv_symm x q)).symm }
    77	  hom_inv_id := by
    78	    ext T v
    79	    exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (rep.homEquiv.symm_apply_apply
    80	      (Over.homMk v rfl : Over.mk (v ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J))
    81	  inv_hom_id := by
    82	    ext T x
    83	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    84	    let g := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    85	    have hga : g.left ≫ J.hom = a := g.w
    86	    refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext F hga ?_
    87	    change F.map (Over.mkCongr hga).op x =
    88	      rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl : Over.mk (g.left ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J)
    89	    rw [← rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x]
    90	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    91	    exact congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl)
    92	
    93	/-! ## The represented rank-one open -/
    94	
    95	/-- The Yoneda range of an open immersion is represented by its source.  Here the range is
    96	identified with the exact divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    97	noncomputable def rankOneDivisorOpenRepresentableBy
    98	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    99	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   100	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor.RepresentableBy
   101	      (divRankOneOpenOver pi h) where
   102	  homEquiv {T} :=
   103	    { toFun := fun y => ⟨y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h, by
   104	        have hy : y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h ∈
   105	            (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj (op T) :=
   106	          ⟨y, rfl⟩
   107	        rw [h.carrier_eq] at hy
   108	        exact hy⟩
   109	      invFun := fun x => Classical.choose

     1	/-

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# At a one-point test, Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity
    10	
    11	DAT-J's `quasiCompact` field reduces — in either coordinate system, see
    12	`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean` and `Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean` — to one
    13	statement `hcl`: **every point of the representing object has its class pulled back along some
    14	field point of the divisor scheme**.  Both of those files record that `hcl` has no producer,
    15	and the routes they name (the Abel image, finite-separable descent) are the expensive ones.
    16	
    17	This file supplies the general fact that reprices the *first* half of that statement, and it
    18	is not about `pic⁰` at all:
    19	
    20	> a Zariski covering sieve of a scheme whose space is a `Subsingleton` **contains the
    21	> identity**, so a locally surjective morphism of presheaves of types is honestly surjective
    22	> on sections there.
    23	
    24	`Spec K` for a field `K` is such a scheme (`Unique (PrimeSpectrum K)` in mathlib), and the
    25	tests `hcl` quantifies over are exactly `overSpec k κ(y)`.  So on the `hcl` side, coverage —
    26	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, which the seam **already assumes** — is not
    27	merely "locally" available at a field point: it gives a section on the nose, with no descent
    28	step and no Abel image.
    29	
    30	## Why the statement is about a `Subsingleton` space and not about fields
    31	
    32	The proof looks at the space only, and it goes through for an arbitrary presheaf of types on
    33	`Scheme`: take a cover refining the sieve (`exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology`), take
    34	the component over the unique point, observe its base map is epi *because the target has at
    35	most one point*, conclude it is an isomorphism (`IsOpenImmersion.isIso`), and use
    36	`Sieve.downward_closed` along its inverse.  Nothing here mentions `pic⁰`, the curve, the
    37	divisor scheme, or the sheaf condition.  Stated in that generality deliberately: it is the
    38	mirror image of `Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`'s
    39	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`, which refutes the `V = ⊥` endpoint by
    40	looking only at the *emptiness* of the space.  Empty spaces kill local surjectivity; one-point
    41	spaces make it free.  Both are facts about the site, not about the Picard functor.
    42	
    43	## What this does NOT do, stated because the temptation here is exactly the audited failure mode
    44	
    45	**It does not discharge `hcl`, and it does not discharge any antecedent.**  What it gives is a
    46	section of the Σ-sheaf over `Spec κ(y)` *in the image of the atlas*, i.e. an index `i` and a
    47	`κ(y)`-point of the `i`-th chart source.  `hcl` asks for a point of `divSchemeOver …` whose
    48	class is `pic0Map C q lam` for the **one fixed** class `lam`.  Two gaps remain and neither is
    49	touched here:
    50	
    51	* the chart source of `mixedParamChart` is `(V i : Scheme)`, an *open of* `(D i).left`, and the
    52	  chart index `i` produced is the one coverage happens to supply — so the point obtained lies in
    53	  a chart of the atlas, not in a single named divisor scheme;
    54	* `hcl`'s `lam` is fixed *before* `y` is quantified, whereas coverage's index varies with the
    55	  point.  Collapsing that quantifier order is the real content of `hcl`, and this file leaves
    56	  it open.
    57	
    58	So the honest reading is: **the "local" in DAT-B's local surjectivity costs nothing at the
    59	tests DAT-J quantifies over.**  That is a subtraction from `hcl`'s price, not a payment of it.
    60	
    61	## Main declarations
    62	
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — a covering sieve of a
    64	  `Subsingleton`-space scheme contains an isomorphism.  The only geometric input.
    65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — hence it contains the identity, i.e. it
    66	  is the top sieve on the nose.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton` — hence local
    68	  surjectivity of an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types is surjectivity on sections
    69	  there.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton` — the `pic⁰`
    71	  reading: at a one-point test, a covering chart family hits **every** section, by a genuine
    72	  index and a genuine point of that chart's source.
    73	-/
    74	
    75	set_option autoImplicit false
    76	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    77	
    78	universe u v
    79	
    80	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    81	
    82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    83	
    84	/-! ## The site fact -/
    85	
    86	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains an isomorphism.**
    87	
    88	Take a cover refining the sieve; its component over the point `x` is an open immersion whose
    89	base map is surjective *because the target is a subsingleton*, hence an isomorphism.
    90	
    91	The `Subsingleton` hypothesis is on the space, and `x` witnesses that it is also nonempty —
    92	both are needed: on the empty scheme the bottom sieve covers
    93	(`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`) and contains no isomorphism at all. -/
    94	theorem exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
    95	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
    96	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X), S.arrows g ∧ IsIso g := by
    97	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology hS
    98	  obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq x
    99	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (𝒰.f i) := 𝒰.map_prop i
   100	  haveI : Epi (𝒰.f i).base := by
   101	    rw [TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]
   102	    exact fun z => ⟨y, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
   103	  exact ⟨𝒰.X i, 𝒰.f i, hle _ _ (Presieve.ofArrows.mk i), IsOpenImmersion.isIso (𝒰.f i)⟩
   104	
   105	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains the identity** —
   106	so on such a scheme "covering" carries no information beyond nonemptiness.
   107	
   108	`Sieve.downward_closed` along the inverse of the isomorphism above. -/
   109	theorem id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
   110	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
   111	    S.arrows (𝟙 X) := by
   112	  obtain ⟨Y, g, hg, hiso⟩ := exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology x S hS
   113	  have h := S.downward_closed hg (inv g)
   114	  rwa [IsIso.inv_hom_id] at h
   115	
   116	/-- **Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity at a one-point test.**
   117	
   118	For an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types on `Scheme`: the image sieve of a section is
   119	covering by hypothesis, hence contains the identity by the previous theorem, and an identity in
   120	the image sieve *is* a preimage of the section.
   121	
   122	No `pic⁰`, no curve, no sheaf condition — this is the counterpart of
   123	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`
   124	(`Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`), which refutes local surjectivity on the *empty* space by
   125	the same kind of purely site-level argument. -/
   126	theorem app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton
   127	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (φ : F ⟶ G)
   128	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology φ]
   129	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)] (x : X) :
   130	    Function.Surjective (φ.app (op X)) := by
   131	  intro s
   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ :=
   133	    id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology x _
   134	      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem Scheme.zariskiTopology φ s)
   135	  exact ⟨t, by simpa using ht⟩
   136	
   137	/-! ## The instances at `Spec` of a field
   138	
   139	Recorded as `example`s rather than restated: both are mathlib instances
   140	(`PrimeSpectrum.instUnique` for a field), and the point of listing them is that the tests
   141	`hcl` quantifies over — `overSpec k κ(y)` — satisfy the hypotheses above with nothing to
   142	prove. -/
   143	
   144	section Field
   145	
   146	variable (K : Type u) [Field K]
   147	
   148	example : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   149	
   150	example : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   151	
   152	end Field
   153	
   154	/-! ## The `pic⁰` reading -/
   155	
   156	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   157	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   158	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   159	
   160	/-- **At a one-point test, a covering chart family hits every section on the nose.**
   161

    22	certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
    23	a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
    24	records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.

    26	## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)
    27	
    28	The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
    29	an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
    30	`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin

    32	`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
    33	stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
    34	that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
    35	making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
    36	instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)
    39	
    40	The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
    41	`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`

    13	statement `hcl`: **every point of the representing object has its class pulled back along some
    14	field point of the divisor scheme**.  Both of those files record that `hcl` has no producer,
    15	and the routes they name (the Abel image, finite-separable descent) are the expensive ones.
    16	
    17	This file supplies the general fact that reprices the *first* half of that statement, and it
    18	is not about `pic⁰` at all:
    19	
    20	> a Zariski covering sieve of a scheme whose space is a `Subsingleton` **contains the
    21	> identity**, so a locally surjective morphism of presheaves of types is honestly surjective
    22	> on sections there.
    23	
    24	`Spec K` for a field `K` is such a scheme (`Unique (PrimeSpectrum K)` in mathlib), and the
    25	tests `hcl` quantifies over are exactly `overSpec k κ(y)`.  So on the `hcl` side, coverage —
    26	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, which the seam **already assumes** — is not
    27	merely "locally" available at a field point: it gives a section on the nose, with no descent
    28	step and no Abel image.
    29	
    30	## Why the statement is about a `Subsingleton` space and not about fields
    31	
    32	The proof looks at the space only, and it goes through for an arbitrary presheaf of types on
    33	`Scheme`: take a cover refining the sieve (`exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology`), take
    34	the component over the unique point, observe its base map is epi *because the target has at
    35	most one point*, conclude it is an isomorphism (`IsOpenImmersion.isIso`), and use
    36	`Sieve.downward_closed` along its inverse.  Nothing here mentions `pic⁰`, the curve, the
    37	divisor scheme, or the sheaf condition.  Stated in that generality deliberately: it is the
    38	mirror image of `Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`'s
    39	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`, which refutes the `V = ⊥` endpoint by
    40	looking only at the *emptiness* of the space.  Empty spaces kill local surjectivity; one-point
    41	spaces make it free.  Both are facts about the site, not about the Picard functor.
    42	
    43	## What this does NOT do, stated because the temptation here is exactly the audited failure mode
    44	
    45	**It does not discharge `hcl`, and it does not discharge any antecedent.**  What it gives is a
    46	section of the Σ-sheaf over `Spec κ(y)` *in the image of the atlas*, i.e. an index `i` and a
    47	`κ(y)`-point of the `i`-th chart source.  `hcl` asks for a point of `divSchemeOver …` whose
    48	class is `pic0Map C q lam` for the **one fixed** class `lam`.  Two gaps remain and neither is
    49	touched here:
    50	
    51	* the chart source of `mixedParamChart` is `(V i : Scheme)`, an *open of* `(D i).left`, and the
    52	  chart index `i` produced is the one coverage happens to supply — so the point obtained lies in
    53	  a chart of the atlas, not in a single named divisor scheme;
    54	* `hcl`'s `lam` is fixed *before* `y` is quantified, whereas coverage's index varies with the
    55	  point.  Collapsing that quantifier order is the real content of `hcl`, and this file leaves
    56	  it open.
    57	
    58	So the honest reading is: **the "local" in DAT-B's local surjectivity costs nothing at the
    59	tests DAT-J quantifies over.**  That is a subtraction from `hcl`'s price, not a payment of it.
    60	
    61	## Main declarations
    62	
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — a covering sieve of a
    64	  `Subsingleton`-space scheme contains an isomorphism.  The only geometric input.
    65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — hence it contains the identity, i.e. it
    66	  is the top sieve on the nose.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton` — hence local
    68	  surjectivity of an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types is surjectivity on sections
    69	  there.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton` — the `pic⁰`
    71	  reading: at a one-point test, a covering chart family hits **every** section, by a genuine
    72	  index and a genuine point of that chart's source.
    73	-/

    82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    84	/-! ## The site fact -/
    85	
    86	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains an isomorphism.**
    87	
    88	Take a cover refining the sieve; its component over the point `x` is an open immersion whose
    89	base map is surjective *because the target is a subsingleton*, hence an isomorphism.
    90	
    91	The `Subsingleton` hypothesis is on the space, and `x` witnesses that it is also nonempty —
    92	both are needed: on the empty scheme the bottom sieve covers
    93	(`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`) and contains no isomorphism at all. -/
    94	theorem exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
    95	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
    96	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X), S.arrows g ∧ IsIso g := by
    97	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology hS
    98	  obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq x
    99	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (𝒰.f i) := 𝒰.map_prop i
   100	  haveI : Epi (𝒰.f i).base := by
   101	    rw [TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]
   102	    exact fun z => ⟨y, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
   103	  exact ⟨𝒰.X i, 𝒰.f i, hle _ _ (Presieve.ofArrows.mk i), IsOpenImmersion.isIso (𝒰.f i)⟩
   104	
   105	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains the identity** —
   106	so on such a scheme "covering" carries no information beyond nonemptiness.
   107	
   108	`Sieve.downward_closed` along the inverse of the isomorphism above. -/
   109	theorem id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
   110	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
   111	    S.arrows (𝟙 X) := by
   112	  obtain ⟨Y, g, hg, hiso⟩ := exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology x S hS
   113	  have h := S.downward_closed hg (inv g)
   114	  rwa [IsIso.inv_hom_id] at h
   115	
   116	/-- **Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity at a one-point test.**
   117	
   118	For an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types on `Scheme`: the image sieve of a section is
   119	covering by hypothesis, hence contains the identity by the previous theorem, and an identity in
   120	the image sieve *is* a preimage of the section.
   121	
   122	No `pic⁰`, no curve, no sheaf condition — this is the counterpart of
   123	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`
   124	(`Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`), which refutes local surjectivity on the *empty* space by
   125	the same kind of purely site-level argument. -/
   126	theorem app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton
   127	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (φ : F ⟶ G)
   128	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology φ]
   129	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)] (x : X) :
   130	    Function.Surjective (φ.app (op X)) := by
   131	  intro s
   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ :=
   133	    id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology x _
   134	      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem Scheme.zariskiTopology φ s)
   135	  exact ⟨t, by simpa using ht⟩

   137	/-! ## The instances at `Spec` of a field
   138	
   139	Recorded as `example`s rather than restated: both are mathlib instances
   140	(`PrimeSpectrum.instUnique` for a field), and the point of listing them is that the tests
   141	`hcl` quantifies over — `overSpec k κ(y)` — satisfy the hypotheses above with nothing to
   142	prove. -/

   145	
   146	variable (K : Type u) [Field K]
   147	
   148	example : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   149	
   150	example : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   151	
   152	end Field

   154	/-! ## The `pic⁰` reading -/
   155	
   156	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   157	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   158	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   159	
   160	/-- **At a one-point test, a covering chart family hits every section on the nose.**
   161	
   162	Given DAT-B's coverage (`ChartsCoverLocally`, the `pic⁰` spelling a producer actually attempts)
   163	and a test whose space has at most one point, every section `s` of the Σ-sheaf over that test
   164	is `f i` applied to a genuine point of the `i`-th chart source — no restriction to a
   165	neighbourhood, no refinement, no descent.
   166	
   167	This is what makes the "local" in B-5/B-6 free at the tests DAT-J's `hcl` quantifies over
   168	(`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean`).  It does **not** produce `hcl`: the index `i` here is
   169	whichever one coverage supplies at `s`, while `hcl` fixes one class `lam` on one divisor scheme
   170	before quantifying over points.  See this file's module docstring for the two surviving gaps. -/
   171	theorem exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton {ι : Type u}
   172	    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   173	    (hcov : ChartsCoverLocally C f)
   174	    {T : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (T : Type u)] (t : T)
   175	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   176	    ∃ (i : ι) (x : T ⟶ X i), (f i).app (op T) x = s := by
   177	  have hid := id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology t _ (hcov T s)
   178	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hid
   179	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hid
   180	  exact ⟨i, x, by simpa using hx⟩
   181	
   182	end AlgebraicGeometry
